summary: Include verse 182 in the reference
rationale: Verse 182 contains gəmḥalqono i goke du semo me iḏi, me riši du quṣro, the first sentence of this quotation. Verse 183 contains Haka lqiṭole ... gməblalle, its second sentence. The automatic suggestion 73/193 describes the later actual throw and is not this quotation.

summary: New sense 2: (Steine) mit der Kammhacke behauen, zurichten
rationale: After breaking the slab into stones, the workers apply a daraġ before handing the stones to masons. This supports surface dressing, not collecting. One attestation.

data.turoyo: Nafiqo barṯo du paša lu sayran. Lqiṭole mu səsyo, zayiʕo, əmmo: “Gquṭeli.”
data.translation: Eines Tages aber ritt die Tochter des Statthalters spazieren; da erhaschte er sie und zog sie vom Pferde herab; sie fürchtete sich und dachte, er werde sie umbringen.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 82/10)

data.turoyo: Omər: "Ḥoṯo, səmləx ḥile aʕli." Əmmo: "Aydarbo?" Omər: "Šləqləx ḥəmṣe, kloṭaʕno, lo koṯe mede b lišoni w hat kləqṭatte b maquzəx."
data.translation: Da sagte er: "Schwester, du hast mir einen Streich gespielt." "Wie so?" fragte sie. Er antwortete: "Du hast Erbsen geröstet, ich lecke und bekomme nichts auf meine Zunge, du aber pickst sie mit deinem Schnabel alle auf."

rationale: Unusual Infectum object suffix -te with explicit beak instrument, beyond four inherited plain picking examples.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (94/18)

data.turoyo: Bəṯr, b ḥamməš daqayəq koqoyəm u šifo, komaqərsile w mqaṭṣile, saymile kefe. Bu daraġ koləqṭənne, bəṯr kobənne lan naḥote. An naḥote ste konəḥtənne w kosaymi ḥaǧat l ʕmara mənne.
data.translation: Nach fünf minnten hebt sich die Steinplatte los. Sie stemmen sieheraus, zerkleinern sie und machen Steine daraus. Diese hauen sie mit der Kammhacke zurecht und übergeben sie dann den Steinmetzen. Diese behauen sie und machen daraus Baumaterial.

rationale: Only example of the new technical sense; full quarrying sequence motivates the meaning.

summary: I Preterit has l-agent coding alongside full zero-marked patients; 24/150 and 58/259 show overt l- agent NPs. Infectum -te indexes peas with b- marking the beak at PrS 82/10.
Gleaning has lqoṭo/laqṭo nominal forms and habitual Infectum-wa luqṭowa. Existing Infectum already explicitly covers gathering ears in stubble, so gleaning is not a new numbered sense.

90/147 Detransitive suppresses the agent and profiles disposition in b-lebo; its two tokens and the inherited Ilyas love example already document the heart construction. Read-only lqiṭ/lebo searches found these existing examples, so no duplicate idiom quotation is added.
Read-only lookup of lqṭ 2 confirms II/III feeding and seed-setting, not stem I gleaning or snatching. Keep the homonym boundary.

PrS 39/51 and39/85 match inherited prs 106/18 and107/32. PrS 39/86 German omits the literal pearl-picking relative clause, so it cannot supply an aligned new quotation. 24/150 and73/183 are already cited.
Confirm whether quarrying lqṭ in 94/18 means dressing the stone surface with repeated blows rather than picking stones out; the daraġ and order of work favor the proposed technical sense.
Are lqoṭo and laqṭo variants of the productive Infinitiv, or is laqṭo a lexicalized task noun?
At 58/259, does -o refer to the chickpea, and does the picking verb entail removal here? German pickte danach leaves the endpoint open.
Can editors supply an explicit aligned translation of the target clause in PrS 39/86 if they want that example?
Taking human patients, predatory catching and rescuing or abducting persons retain the existing broad taking/catching sense; no 'swallow' meaning follows merely from German verschlang.
